name: Breast Cancer Now (SoGive, 2021)
summary: Funds breast cancer research in the UK and runs support services and campaigns. SoGive's estimate of the cost per year of healthy life gained by UK breast cancer research as a whole (1970–2010), which it uses for the charity, rebuilt from SoGive's analysis.

source.title: Breast Cancer Now: SoGive rating and analysis
source.license: No licence on the page. SoGive's data terms (sogive.org/doc/getourdata.html, archived September 2019): data for charity analysis is free with attribution to SoGive; use in apps needs a licence, free for low-intensity use, on condition that users are told the source of impact assessments with a link back to SoGive. This model cites SoGive and links its page.

resources.title: SoGive, Breast Cancer Now analysis
resources.note: SoGive's charity page (its analysis text); SoGive publishes no spreadsheet for it, so the model is built from the figures stated in the text, each quoted on its row. Rated "Not Recommended (tentative)". The page carries no date; it cites the charity's 2019–20 annual report and NCRI's 2020 data package, so the date here (2021) is our estimate.

resources.title: Glover et al. (2014), Estimating the returns to UK publicly funded cancer-related research in terms of the net value of improved health outcomes, BMC Medicine 12:99

sections.title: UK cancer research spending on breast cancer, 1970–2009
sections.explainer: SoGive can't trace Breast Cancer Now's own research to health gains, so it uses the average return on all UK breast cancer research, from Glover et al. (2014), and assumes the charity's research is about average.

sections.title: From pounds per healthy year to healthy years per dollar
sections.explainer: charityevals' steps after SoGive's bottom line: pounds to dollars, and the delay between paying for research and the health it brings, discounted at the shared rate.

sections.title: Staff pay below market
sections.explainer: charityevals' step, not the evaluator's: with credit by share of resources on, staff's pay below what they could earn elsewhere counts as an in-kind contribution and gets its share of the outcome. Off by default.

rows.label: UK cancer research spending, 1970–2009 (£)

source.title: SoGive, charity analysis
source.quote: They also estimate total research expenditure from 1970 to 2009 (see Additional File 1), which comes out to £15.1bn.

rows.explainer: From Glover et al. (2014), the research taken to produce the health gains of 1991–2010.

rows.label: Share of that spending labelled by cancer type

source.title: SoGive, charity analysis
source.quote: the proportion of labelled expenditure across 2002 to 2010 is calculated as 40%

rows.explainer: From the National Cancer Research Institute's 2020 data package, 2002–2009.

rows.label: Breast cancer's share of the labelled spending

source.title: SoGive, charity analysis
source.quote: Of the proportion of labelled expenditure, breast cancer-related research accounts for an estimated 19% across the time period.

rows.label: Breast cancer's share of the unlabelled spending

source.title: SoGive, charity analysis
source.quote: we can estimate lower and upper bounds - i.e none of the unlabelled expenditure is related to breast cancer or all of it is

rows.explainer: SoGive gives only the two bounds, none and all of it, so its result is a range (£1,000 to £8,800 per healthy year). The central value is ours: the unlabelled spending split like the labelled, 19%.

rows.label: Breast cancer's share of all UK cancer research spending
Healthy years gained from breast cancer screening and treatment, 1991–2010

source.title: SoGive, charity analysis
source.quote: the combined estimate for which is 1.155m QALYs gained

rows.explainer: Quality-adjusted life years gained from the key advances in screening and treatment, from Glover et al. (2014), Table 2.

rows.label: Cost per healthy year gained (£)
rows.explainer: SoGive: "this implies the cost-effectiveness of breast cancer research is around £1,000 - £8,800 per QALY gained". The central value comes from our middle share above. SoGive counts only gains up to 2010 from research up to 2009, and argues later gains wouldn't change the verdict.

rows.label: US dollars per pound, 2021
rows.explainer: charityevals' step: SoGive's figure is in pounds; the site counts per dollar, so the pounds are converted at the year's average exchange rate (shared fact). SoGive doesn't say in which year's prices Glover et al.'s spending is stated; we convert at the rate of the year the analysis was written.

rows.label: Discount rate on future health
rows.explainer: The shared discount rate (Your values). SoGive doesn't discount, so the evaluator view pins it at 0.

rows.label: Years from paying for research to the health it brings

source.title: Glover et al. (2014), BMC Medicine 12:99
source.note: Estimates a lag of about 15 years between cancer research spending and its health gains (not checked against the paper's text: the publisher's page asked for sign-in). The range, 10 to 20 years, is our judgment.

rows.explainer: A donation today pays for research whose benefits arrive years later; the same study SoGive relies on puts the lag at about 15 years.

rows.label: Share of Breast Cancer Now's spending that goes to research

source.title: Breast Cancer Now, Annual Report and Accounts 2019–20
source.page: Notes 4 and 5a (expenditure on raising funds and on charitable activities)
source.quote: Research £14,611k; total expenditure £39,651k (raising funds £17,032k, charitable activities £22,619k), 2020

rows.explainer: SoGive's figure is per pound of research; a donation also pays for fundraising, support services and campaigning. Research was £14.6m of £39.7m in 2019–20, 36.85%.

rows.label: Healthy years per dollar donated to the charity
rows.explainer: A QALY gained counts as one healthy year, the same as a DALY averted; only the research share of a donation is credited with them.

rows.label: Staff pay as a share of program cost
rows.explainer: Default for a charity that mostly gives grants or buys goods: staff are a small part of the cost. Our judgment; we haven't seen this charity's breakdown.

rows.label: Pay gap versus comparable jobs elsewhere
rows.explainer: UK charity staff earn somewhat less than in comparable private-sector jobs. Our judgment.

rows.label: Salary forgone by staff per dollar of cost (in-kind donation)
Share of the full cost paid in cash
rows.explainer: With credit by share of resources, staff's forgone pay counts as part of the cost, and staff get their share of the outcome. Off, this is 100%.

rows.label: Healthy years per dollar donated
rows.explainer: The figure per dollar above; with credit by share of resources, times the share of the full cost paid in cash (staff's forgone pay is the rest).
